newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks inch to slightly higher close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks inch to slightly higher close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks inched to a slightly higher close on Monday, with a record-breaking performance by Hutchison Whampoa offset by profit-taking in HSBC Holdings, brokers said.
"Trading was quite selective," said a broker with a small regional house. "Hutchison was bid up but there was more profit-taking in HSBC."
The Hang Seng Index closed 8.47 points, or 0.05 percent, higher at 15,666.59.
The index opened down at 15,627.03 but quickly climbed to positive territory, where it stayed for the rest of the day.
Turnover remained a robust HK$16.90 billion, although down slightly from Friday's HK$18.96 billion.
Brokers said retail investors continued to dominate trading.
Hutchison, which has been an in-line-with-the-market performer for the past 18 months, was one of the most actively traded stocks, analysts said.

The share leaped to an all time high of HK$72.50 then eased to close HK$2.00 up at HK$71.75. The company last week raised US$2 billion in a bond issue, which will be largely used for planned 1997 capital expenditure and debt refinancing, said Chris Wilmot, associate director at Indosuez W.I. Carr.

Banking giant HSBC Holdings slipped HK$3.00 to close at HK$259.00 on relatively heavy trade of HK$657.79 million. Subsidiary Hang Seng Bank was unchanged at HK$114.00. Bank of East Asia, which will report its first-half results on Friday, jumped HK$0.60 to HK$32.50.

The commercial and the industrial sector led the market, followed by properties. New World Development led the property sector higher, advancing HK$1.25 to HK$50.75. Cheung Kong put on HK$0.75 to HK$76.50.
"Cheung Kong is my top pick among the developers," said Adrian Ngan, director of Peregrine Securities.
Shenzhen International was the most actively traded issue. The share rose to match its record high of HK$1.92, then fell back to close HK$0.22 higher at HK$1.89 on trade of HK$679.67 million.
The company recently placed 58 million new shares to new investors, China Everbright Financial Holdings Ltd and ASG Capital Ltd.
Trading in July Hang Seng Index futures was relatively active. The contract, which expires on Wednesday, closed unchanged at 15,680, a slight premium to the cash market.
